stated_count: 'eight crocodiles' among ~14 animal mummies transferred from Natural History Society of Montreal; Ferrier 1859 donation incl. 'four small mummified crocodiles'; 1926 transfer notebook '8 Mummified Crocodiles Egypt'
stated_count_source: Lawson, B. 2016, 'Egyptian Mummies at the Redpath Museum: Unravelling the History of McGill University's Collection', Fontanus (McGill Library), pp. 2-4 and endnote on 1926 notebook
possible_additional_holdings: Up to 8 crocodile mummies per Lawson 2016 (historic counts); only 2 individually identified (2725.01, 2725.02) in ÉTS 2024 report. Current total not verified.
notes: Lawson (Redpath Curator of World Cultures) 2016, on McGill domain: 'There are three human mummies and approximately twenty animal mummies (cats, crocodiles, and birds) in the Redpath World Cultures Collection'. Crocodiles came via James Ferrier (acquired on 1859 Nile trip; Maabdeh visited) and the defunct Natural History Society of Montreal. Redpath 'Permanent displays' page mentions 'several mummified animals'. No online collection DB. Redpath is removing human remains from display 2026-27 (3rd-floor page).
